sections.heading: 1. What Ostrevia is and what it is used for
sections.text:
Ostrevia contains the active substance lumiravostat. It works by calming the part of the immune system that causes inflammation of the skin.
Ostrevia is used to treat adults with long-lasting (chronic) hand eczema that is moderate to severe, when strong steroid creams have not worked well enough or cannot be used.

sections.heading: 2. What you need to know before you take Ostrevia
Do not take Ostrevia
Warnings and precautions
sections.text:
Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before taking Ostrevia if you:
have an infection, or keep getting infections. Ostrevia can lower your body’s ability to fight infections.
have had TB or been in close contact with someone with TB. Your doctor will test you for TB before you start.
have had cancer, or get new skin growths
have had blood clots in your legs or lungs
have liver problems
Tell your doctor straight away if you get a fever, chills, cough, leg pain or swelling, chest pain or sudden shortness of breath.
You will have blood tests before you start and while you take Ostrevia.

sections.heading: Children and adolescents
sections.text: Do not give this medicine to children and adolescents under 18 years because it has not been studied in this age group.

sections.heading: Other medicines and Ostrevia
sections.text: Tell your doctor or pharmacist if you are taking, have recently taken or might take any other medicines, especially medicines for fungal infections (such as ketoconazole) or tuberculosis (such as rifampicin).

sections.heading: Pregnancy and breast-feeding
sections.text:
Do not take Ostrevia if you are pregnant. It may harm your unborn baby. If you can become pregnant, use effective contraception while taking Ostrevia and for 4 weeks after your last dose.
Do not breast-feed while taking Ostrevia and for 4 days after your last dose.

sections.heading: Driving and using machines
sections.text: Ostrevia is not expected to affect your ability to drive or use machines.

sections.heading: Ostrevia contains sodium
sections.text: This medicine contains less than 1 mmol sodium (23 mg) per tablet, that is to say essentially ‘sodium-free’.

sections.heading: 3. How to take Ostrevia
sections.text:
Always take this medicine exactly as your doctor or pharmacist has told you. Check with your doctor or pharmacist if you are not sure.
The recommended dose is one 10 mg tablet once a day. Your doctor may increase it to one 25 mg tablet once a day after 12 weeks. Swallow the tablet whole, with or without food.

sections.heading: If you take more Ostrevia than you should
sections.text: Talk to a doctor or pharmacist straight away.

sections.heading: If you forget to take Ostrevia
sections.text: Take it as soon as you remember on the same day. Do not take a double dose to make up for a forgotten tablet.

sections.heading: If you stop taking Ostrevia
sections.text:
Talk to your doctor before you stop. Your eczema may come back.
If you have any further questions on the use of this medicine, ask your doctor or pharmacist.

sections.heading: 4. Possible side effects
sections.text:
Like all medicines, this medicine can cause side effects, although not everybody gets them.
Serious side effects. Tell your doctor straight away if you notice: signs of a serious infection (fever, chills, cough, burning when passing urine); signs of a blood clot (leg pain or swelling, chest pain, sudden shortness of breath).
Very common (may affect more than 1 in 10 people): common cold.
Common (may affect up to 1 in 10 people): headache, feeling sick (nausea), acne, shingles (herpes zoster), changes in blood tests.
Uncommon (may affect up to 1 in 100 people): pneumonia, skin infection (cellulitis), blood clots in the legs or lungs.

sections.heading: Reporting of side effects
sections.text: If you get any side effects, talk to your doctor or pharmacist. This includes any possible side effects not listed in this leaflet. You can also report side effects directly via the national reporting system listed in Appendix V. By reporting side effects you can help provide more information on the safety of this medicine.

sections.heading: 5. How to store Ostrevia
sections.text:
Keep this medicine out of the sight and reach of children.
Do not use this medicine after the expiry date which is stated on the carton and blister after EXP. The expiry date refers to the last day of that month.
This medicine does not require any special storage conditions.
Do not throw away any medicines via wastewater or household waste. Ask your pharmacist how to throw away medicines you no longer use. These measures will help protect the environment.

sections.heading: 6. Contents of the pack and other information
What Ostrevia contains
sections.text:
The active substance is lumiravostat. Each film-coated tablet contains 10 mg or 25 mg of lumiravostat.
The other ingredients are microcrystalline cellulose, croscarmellose sodium, magnesium stearate, hypromellose, titanium dioxide (E171) and, in the 25 mg tablet, iron oxide yellow (E172). See section 2 "Ostrevia contains sodium".

sections.heading: What Ostrevia looks like and contents of the pack
sections.text: Ostrevia 10 mg are white, round tablets marked "HR" and "10". Ostrevia 25 mg are yellow, oval tablets marked "HR" and "25". Packs of 28 or 84 tablets in blisters. Not all pack sizes may be marketed.

sections.heading: What is the most important information I should know about OSTREVIA?
sections.text:
OSTREVIA can cause serious side effects, including:
Serious infections. OSTREVIA lowers the ability of your immune system to fight infections. Some people have had serious infections that needed hospital care or caused death. Tell your healthcare provider right away if you have a fever, sweating, chills, cough, or burning when you pass urine.
Cancer. Some people taking OSTREVIA have had lymphoma and skin cancer. Tell your healthcare provider if you have ever had any type of cancer.
Blood clots. Blood clots in the legs or lungs can happen. Stop taking OSTREVIA and get medical help right away if you have leg pain or swelling, chest pain, or sudden shortness of breath.

sections.heading: What is OSTREVIA?
sections.text:
OSTREVIA is a prescription medicine for adults with long-lasting (chronic) hand eczema. It is used when the eczema is moderate to severe and steroid creams or ointments have not worked well enough.
It is not known if OSTREVIA is safe and effective in children.

sections.heading: Who should not take OSTREVIA?
sections.text: Do not take OSTREVIA if you are allergic to lumiravostat or any of the ingredients in OSTREVIA. See the end of this Medication Guide for a list of the ingredients.

sections.heading: What should I tell my healthcare provider before taking OSTREVIA?
sections.text:
Before taking OSTREVIA, tell your healthcare provider about all of your medical conditions, including if you:
have an infection, or keep getting infections
have had tuberculosis (TB) or been in close contact with someone with TB
have had a blood clot
have liver problems
are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. OSTREVIA may harm your unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for 4 weeks after your last dose.
are breastfeeding or plan to breastfeed. Do not breastfeed during treatment and for 4 days after your last dose.
Tell your healthcare provider about all the medicines you take, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins and herbal supplements.

sections.heading: How should I take OSTREVIA?
sections.text:
Take OSTREVIA exactly as your healthcare provider tells you.
Take OSTREVIA 1 time each day, with or without food.
Swallow the tablet whole. Do not split, crush or chew it.
If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember that day. Do not take 2 doses on the same day.

sections.heading: What are the possible side effects of OSTREVIA?
sections.text:
OSTREVIA can cause serious side effects. See "What is the most important information I should know about OSTREVIA?"
The most common side effects of OSTREVIA include: common cold, headache, nausea and acne.
These are not all the possible side effects of OSTREVIA.

sections.heading: How should I store OSTREVIA?
sections.text:
Store OSTREVIA at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C).
Keep OSTREVIA in the bottle it comes in.
Keep OSTREVIA and all medicines out of the reach of children.

sections.heading: General information about the safe and effective use of OSTREVIA.
sections.text: Medicines are sometimes prescribed for purposes other than those listed in a Medication Guide. Do not use OSTREVIA for a condition for which it was not prescribed. Do not give OSTREVIA to other people, even if they have the same symptoms that you have. You can ask your pharmacist or healthcare provider for information about OSTREVIA that is written for health professionals.

sections.heading: What are the ingredients in OSTREVIA?
sections.text:
Active ingredient: lumiravostat
Inactive ingredients: microcrystalline cellulose, croscarmellose sodium, magnesium stearate, hypromellose and titanium dioxide. The 25 mg tablet also contains iron oxide yellow.
